main_text.p: [illegible, ~12 letters] Syr. Anxietas, angustia, dolor, 2. ad Cor. 2.4. Græc. ἀνιαρία.

אנף אנפא & אף, אפא Ch. & Syr. Facies, Vultus, Nasus. Plur. אנפין, אנפי & אפין, אפי. Syr. ܐܦܐ, ܐܦܝ ܥܠ ܐܦܝ. In facie, superficie, super: מאפי A' facie, Ante: ܩܕܡ. Circa, circiter, Act. 10.3. Matth. 26.39.67: ܥܠ ܐܦܐ. Pro, propter, ad Roman. 4.8. 1. ad Corinth. 13.12.
[illegible, ~6 letters] Facies portæ, i.e. Velamé, ad Hebr. 10.20.
אנפלין Ch. Penetralia, Conclavia, Tabernacula, Cant. 4.12. Sic Hebræi quoque explicant per אוהל, vel בתי שוקים Tentoria, vel Domus epularum, convivio-rum. Græcè τωυλων & πυλεων, Atrium.
אנץ Ch. Incitare, instigare, stimulare, Partic. plur. mascul. דאנצין Quæ stimulant, Eccl. 12.12.
אנק Ch. Gemuit, ingemuit, suspiravit. Idem quod אנה, mutato ה in ק. Ithpeh. אדנק & Ithpah. אדנק Idem.
אניק, אניקא, אניקי Ch. Gemitus, anxietas, calamitas, afflictio, angustia.
אינקא Ch. Nomen avis juxta quosdam, Esth. 1. 2. in Targ. sec. Plur. אנקין Ibid. sub finem illius versus.
אונקלא Ch. Uncus, uncinus, hamus. Plural. אונקלין, Esth. 1.6. & אנקלין Exod. 26.36. in T. Hierosol.
אנש אנשא Ch. & Syr. Homo, Mortalis. Per Aphæresin נש, נשא, quomodo usurpatur, quando nomini

page.notes: Hebrew, Syriac and Greek forms are transcribed as far as legible; some Syriac and Hebrew vowel-pointed forms and the first line are uncertain. Line beginning "[illegible]" is a partly damaged Syriac word at the top; the Syriac Ch./Syr. forms in the second paragraph are approximate.
